title: Long NOC — Northrop Grumman, Active Iran Military Operations + Nuclear Modernization Cycle
entry: Initiate $558–570 (current zone; May 29 price ~$561). Scale: 70% at current, 30% add on confirmation of Iran MoU language-gap failure with official diplomatic statement OR another IRGC military incident. No macro pre-condition required — defense appropriations are structurally insulated from PCE, Fed, and SpaceX IPO capital-drain dynamics.
stop_loss: $535 daily close (~4.7% below entry midpoint $562) — implies formal Iran ceasefire confirmed with Hormuz reopening timeline AND WTI drops decisively below $85, simultaneously removing the Iran war premium from the defense sector AND triggering a multi-sector risk-on rotation that compresses NOC's geopolitical premium
targets: $590 — Iran operations continue through Warsh June FOMC; DoD AI-enabled ISR budget supplements confirmed; defense sector maintains war premium; +5.2%
$625 — B-21 Raider production rate increase authorized in FY2027 NDAA supplemental; GBSD Phase 3 contract milestone announced; NOC Q2 FY2026 earnings beat (late July); +11.4%
$665 — Full Iran military duration premium expansion + nuclear modernization funding cycle; NOC total backlog reaches $90B+; international NATO partner orders expand; +18.4%
catalyst: IRGC navy fired warning shots at four vessels near the Strait of Hormuz on May 29 morning — the same day the Iran MoU language-gap negotiations are stalled with VP Vance calling signing 'still TBD.' This is the second consecutive day of IRGC military posturing (after May 28 US strikes on Iranian facilities), confirming the Iran conflict is in an active military-exchange phase, not a pre-ceasefire wind-down. Northrop Grumman's platforms are directly engaged: the E-2D Advanced Hawkeye provides carrier-based early warning for US Navy Group operations in the Persian Gulf region; the B-21 Raider represents the next generation of strategic deterrence being deployed in response to Iran's nuclear stockpile posture; and the GBSD (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent) nuclear missile modernization — the largest single defense program at $100B+ lifetime value — is directly informed by the Iran and Russian nuclear threat environment.
thesis:
Northrop Grumman occupies a unique position in the defense complex: it dominates the two highest-priority US defense programs that are directly driven by the Iran-Russia dual nuclear threat — B-21 Raider stealth bomber and GBSD intercontinental ballistic missile modernization. Unlike diversified defense contractors (LMT, RTX), NOC's program mix is heavily weighted toward systems that are immune to political budget debates: nuclear modernization and strategic bombers are existential deterrence systems that no administration can cancel without geopolitical consequences. The ITA ETF (currently active in the portfolio) provides broad aerospace-and-defense exposure; NOC provides concentrated exposure to the programs with the most direct Iran nuclear-threat correlation.

The B-21 Raider is NOC's flagship growth program: 9 aircraft have been delivered as of April 2026, with full-rate production decision expected Q3 2026. The program is funded at approximately $100B over 100 aircraft; each unit revenue exceeds $700M. The full-rate production trigger would be the single largest single-program revenue commitment in NOC's history, expected to be announced in the June–August window. Simultaneously, the GBSD program (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent, replacing the aging Minuteman III ICBM fleet) reached a major milestone in Q1 2026 when engineering and manufacturing development was formally approved by the Air Force. At $96B lifetime value, GBSD represents 60% of NOC's projected backlog growth through 2030. Both programs move forward regardless of whether Iran signs or doesn't sign — they are funded on threat assessment, not event-specific budgets.

The portfolio construction rationale is diversification from the existing AI-technology-heavy long book. NOC is the only single-name defense play in the current opportunity slate; ITA (active) is a broad ETF that diversifies across 30+ companies. NOC's revenue profile has zero correlation to AI capex cycles, zero correlation to PCE or Fed rate signals, and zero correlation to SpaceX IPO capital rotation dynamics. If DELL's 39% gap and NVDA's AI rally attract fund flows away from defensives on any given day, NOC's fundamental thesis is entirely unchanged. This counter-cyclical quality makes it a stabilizer for a book that has become progressively more concentrated in AI-related names since May 21.
bull_case: Iran MoU language gap hardens into full collapse — IRGC signals no agreement on uranium stockpile terms; US Congress fast-tracks emergency defense appropriations supplemental with $30–50B specifically for Navy anti-ship missile replenishment (Raytheon SM-6, NOC Fire Scout), Air Force B-21 accelerated delivery, and nuclear command-and-control upgrades. B-21 full-rate production decision announced ahead of schedule (June rather than September). NOC Q2 FY2026 earnings (late July) beat on backlog expansion above $88B. Stock to $625–665. Tail: NATO formally expands NOC's international defense AI and ISR platform license to three additional European nations — confirms NOC as the NATO-interoperable surveillance and deterrence platform provider.
bear_case: Iran ceasefire formally signed; Hormuz reopens; WTI falls to $82–85; broad market risk-on rotates out of defensives into AI-technology names. NOC's geopolitical premium compresses by 8–12%; stock falls to $515–535. Stop at $535 triggered. Structural risk: Congressional budget negotiations result in defense top-line reduction in FY2027 NDAA, specifically targeting the nuclear modernization programs NOC depends on. B-21 production rate is cut from 12 to 8 aircraft per year — reduces forward revenue visibility by $2.8B annually.
invalidation: $535 daily close, OR formal Iran ceasefire signed with Hormuz reopening timeline confirmed AND WTI closes below $85 on the signed deal, OR Congressional appropriations freeze on B-21 and GBSD programs specifically
